what_this_is: Every enforcement artifact in this repo, with who runs it and when it was last SEEN TO FAIL. Enforced by scripts/check_gate_registry.py, which re-derives `wired_by` from the runner roots rather than reading it back, and refuses a gate-shaped file that has no row here. R9 (2026-08-25) adds the second half of that discipline: a row whose implementation READS Rust/Lean source must declare in `source_scan` HOW it reads it, and a `raw-lines` scanner may not claim soundness -- because a count over raw text counts comments, and in this tree the comments are the `// SOUNDNESS:` notes the rules demand, so such a gate moves the WRONG WAY on a genuine fix.

columns.path: the artifact (empty for legs and suite rows)
columns.claims: soundness|quality|hygiene|evidence|none -- a soundness row must be demonstrated or waived
columns.wired_by: re-derived, not trusted: the runners that invoke it
columns.demonstrated: the last time a mutation made it say no, pinned by R7 to the sha256 of the file it demonstrated: `path` for a gate/battery, `implemented_by` for a leg/suite-row that has no path of its own. `inherited_from` DELEGATES that pin to another row, and R7 requires that row to pin the very same file. An empty script_sha256 is not a pin.
columns.waiver: owner + expiry + reason, for a row that is not demonstrated yet
columns.source_scan: how the implementation reads Rust/Lean SOURCE, re-derived by R9: lexed (comments and string literals blanked before matching) | raw-lines (matches prose too -- REFUSED for a soundness row) | digest (hash/parse, not a text match). Absent when the row reads no source.
columns.implemented_by: for a leg/suite-row, the file the gate actually lives in -- the subject of R3's runner edge and of R7's freshness pin

retired_columns.id: the retired artifact's former row id
retired_columns.path: the file, which must NO LONGER EXIST (R8)
retired_columns.superseded_by: live, WIRED row ids that carry the property now -- re-derived by R8, never read back; empty only with enforces_nothing:true
retired_columns.evidence: the verbatim output that measurement produced

rows.note: WHY `evidence` AND NOT `soundness`. This gate does not assert anything about the kernel. It asserts that data/crystal_a0_a6_probe.json -- a TRANSCRIPTION, re-minted 2026-08-25 from A0 4-of-6/A6 3-of-4 to 5-of-6/4-of-4 with no compiler run -- still agrees with the nine committed records it cites. It never runs trustc, never seals a driver, never reads a dump: if a cited record is itself wrong, this gate is green and wrong with it. What it refuses is DRIFT between the probe and its sources, which is the failure the re-mint would otherwise have shipped -- a file asserting `each verdict is transcribed from a named committed record` that nothing re-derived. Idempotent by construction: the generator IS the checker (`--mint` writes what the default mode requires). The two transcription stamps (date, clean HEAD) are CARRIED rather than re-derived -- otherwise the gate reddens on the next commit for no reason -- but both are validated, and the sha must resolve to a real commit.

rows.note: MEASURED 2026-08-25, lane LGATE, and it is a HAZARD, not a defect in what the gate CHECKS: `--selftest`'s REAL-TREE arm writes to the tracked file `crates/clean-kernel/src/env/snapshot.rs` and restores it in a `finally`. Observed dirty within ~0.5 s of launch, restored on exit, 14/14 arms green. One of the two writes is `pub fn smuggle(env: &mut E, d: D) { ... }`, which DOES NOT COMPILE. Both this script and scripts/check_add_decl_ratchet.py (same arm shape) are wired into the pre-push HOOK, whose own header asserts "NEVER MUTATES. No leg writes to the worktree" -- that sentence is false, measured. CONSEQUENCE, reproduced not hypothesised: a `scripts/local_gate.sh --fast` run in this worktree compiled clean-kernel while a hook run was in flight and died with `error[E0425]: cannot find type `E` ... snapshot.rs:317`, printing `LOCAL GATE: FAIL - soundness certificate`. That is a red no pusher caused, in the exact class the hook exists to prevent. The arm's VALUE is real (it is the falsification that justified the lexing rewrite) and its meaning is a property of the real file's CONTENT, not of the real PATH, so the repair is to seed a temp tree with those bytes -- a design change owned by the lane that wrote the arm. Recorded here so the next lane does not re-derive it from a mystery compile error.

The question asked was whether the Cargo.toml / Cargo.lock / clean-kernel-Cargo.toml digests drift on unrelated dependency bumps (in which case they are the wrong identity, per the canary-pin precedent) or whether the 2026-08-10-pristine numbers really were measured against a different program. So the drift is inside the benched program, re-pinning would certify 2026-08-10 numbers for a different binary, and the gate is doing its job. ONE cause WAS fixed: `.gitignore`'s bare `logs/` (a Pulse-runtime rule) also matched reports/benchmarks/publication/<run>/logs/, so the three REQUIRED stderr logs were recorded in current.json with sha256 and byte counts and NEVER COMMITTED -- unfixable by re-running the suite, and the reason those three errors would have survived any fresh run. .gitignore now un-excludes that directory, and the checker distinguishes 'nobody produced it' from 'git refuses to store it', naming the pattern and line. COUNT AFTER THIS LANE: 12 errors, not 10, and the two new ones are honest and self-inflicted by design -- `scripts/check_benchmark_publication.py` is itself a CANONICAL INPUT, so editing the checker moves its own pinned digest. rows.note: ON-DEMAND soundness gate for the Trust flip (MIR derived from trust-ir replacing rustc's built MIR). Invariant: no function present in both the control and the flipped build gains a reference to a drop symbol (drop_glue, drop_in_place, Arc/Rc drop_slow, a direct <T as Drop>::drop, dealloc/deallocate -- counted through outlined bodies and one-instruction thunks), and no function only in the arm references one at all -- never explainable -- and every other per-function difference is named, with a reason, in an --explained file. It exists because every earlier check of the flip (crate totals, the symbol set, the trust-ir comparator) passed a double drop in TypeChecker::infer_type: the extra call is a new relocation inside an existing function, visible only per function. kind=battery and wired_by=[] deliberately: it is run BY HAND against a control/arm pair of built objects, and each arm is a Trust build that needs a ~28 GB corpus dump (the lane's figure, not re-measured by this row), so no push-path runner can supply its input. R3 names battery or tool as the classification for an enforcement artifact no runner invokes, and tool would be false: this asserts an invariant. NOT gated by anything: that a flip is burned in with this before it is trusted is an open process item, not a property this row can enforce. Usage: python3 scripts/crystal_object_burnin.py CONTROL ARM [--explained F.json] [--json OUT.json] [--cache-dir DIR]; CONTROL/ARM are an .rlib, one object or a directory of objects. Cost measured 2026-09-23 with --show-all-symbols: the O0 pair 32.7 s wall and 0.55 GB peak RSS cold, the O3 cu=1 pair 24.3 s and 0.42 GB cold (objdump dominates). Burn in at codegen-units=1. At codegen-units>1 per-function identity is the wrong question: partitioning and ThinLTO import move with ANY MIR change. Measured 2026-09-24 on clean-kernel O3 cu=16: two controls agree in all 13,792 functions; the flip that is object-identical over every function at cu=1 keeps the members of only 3 of 16 units, and after the two ThinLTO normalisations (the `.llvm.<hash>` promotion suffix and promoted `_anon.<hash>.<n>` constants, which alone had made 5,800 functions differ and 2,278 'gain' drops) 709 functions still differ and 127 gain drop references, every one of them in the 13 reshuffled units; inside the 3 units whose members are identical, 0 drops are gained and the 7 residual differences are inlining changes. Behaviour at cu=16 is judged by scripts/crystal_kernel_test_battery.py instead. Known limits are in the script's docstring: layout-local labels are renamed, so a switch of WHICH anonymous constant a function loads is invisible; data sections (vtables with their drop entries included) are not compared; a drop reached through an ordinary non-thunk helper counts against the helper, not the caller; and a new codegen-unit copy that drops no more than the most-dropping control copy passes.

Run over two lowerings of the SAME crate differing by ONE producer arm that adds 16 lowered bodies (laneMKD vs laneMKG/wcfull): agree 1371, differ 4790, agreement 0.222529 -- and the disagreements include bodies that are STRUCTURALLY IDENTICAL, e.g. <AppArgsIter<'a> as Clone>::clone, same four instructions, differing only func.7530->7534 / struct.957->983. Until then its verdicts are meaningful only between artifacts whose numbering already coincides -- exactly the case where the question does not arise. REPAIRED 2026-08-27, same day: the channel now normalises global ids through a SHARED BIJECTION across the whole artifact pair (@func.N / struct.N / enum.N / functy.N / global.N / closure_ty.N). It is a bijection, not an erasure -- each id must map to exactly one id and vice versa, GLOBALLY -- so consistent renumbering is absorbed while a changed call target still conflicts. source_scan.note: Reads Rust SOURCE only through scripts/rust_modules.py (since 2026-11-01 the module walk this gate, check_cargo_test_selectors and verify_runner share, derived here as a --pinned-inputs file with its arms and the lexer), which follows module items and item-level include! over code blanked by R9's reference lexer imported from scripts/check_add_decl_ratchet.py (strip_noncode for the structure, strip_comments_keep_strings at the same offsets for the `#[path = "..."]` and include! values, which ARE string literals). R9 accepts that stripper in scripts/rust_modules.py -- a derived input this script's code names, whose code calls strip_noncode -- not in this script; since the 2026-11-01 review it no longer credits the reference lexer itself, which this script pins but never calls (and which its first cut found first). Where that lexer reads a span otherwise than rustc_lexer -- a nested block comment, a '\u{..}' or '\x..' char literal -- the span is blanked as rustc reads it and the file lexed again; one it cannot repair (an unterminated nested comment), or brackets that do not balance, leave the file UNREAD and refused. A `mod` inside a comment or a string literal is not code; attributes are bracket-balanced #[..] groups found in code, so a #[path] inside a string is not one; a `path =` value the strict form cannot read (an escape, a cfg_attr) makes the item unresolvable for this gate rather than guessed, as does a cfg the host facts do not decide true on the item that owns a block (a fn, impl or const) for every mod and include! in it. A raw-text prefilter (a `mod` then `;` before any `{`, or an include!) decides only WHICH files CERTAIN lexes: on every root the three callers read its answer equals the unfiltered walk's.

The verdict logic (scripts/frontend_merge_suite_report.py) runs its arms over RECORDED cargo output FIRST on every local_gate invocation: a `test result: FAILED` line is RED; a binary that dies before its result line is RED; a target cargo never ran is NOT_RUN and red; a target cargo lists under `error: N targets failed` is RED even beside an ok line; a doctest failure is attributed to the doc target; a leg that exits non-zero with no target attributed a failure is red (fail-closed, never 'probably fine'); a zero-test bin or doctest-free crate is EMPTY, never GREEN, while a LIB or INTEGRATION target that passes zero tests, or any target whose every test is ignored, is RED -- a vacuous pass is not a pass (added by the 2026-09-25 review, which replayed the real run log with the clean-elab lib's result line rewritten to `0 passed; ...; 11976 ignored`: before the fix it read EMPTY and the suite said green, after it the lib reads RED and the suite exits 1); an over-budget lib is flagged but never offered to the slow-list; two packages sharing a target name are refused; and the slow-list refuses an under-budget row, a stale row and an unmeasured row, while a SLOW target is printed rather than hidden. REPLAYED 2026-09-25 over the REAL cargo output of the first unfiltered run (2026-09-25, frontend crates as this package forked them): as run it reads red=1 (clean-parser parse_parity) and exits 1; the run log cut at line 9,000 (a leg that died) reads not_run=209, exit 1; with parse_parity's FAILED result line deleted it still reads RED (cargo's `targets failed` list), exit 1; with every trace of the failure scrubbed but the leg's exit 101 kept it reads the target NOT_RUN, exit 1. rows.note: P0_SOUND round 2 (2026-09-24). Rule 0 of the Lean kernel-theory profile admits a native reducer only when it is on LEAN_PROFILE_DIFFERENTIAL_REDUCERS, and this battery is what keeps a name on that list honest. It loads the pinned toolchain's own Init .oleans, fires every allowlisted reducer on a battery of literal inputs built from the head's telescope, and requires each result to be well typed at the head's type and definitionally equal to the head applied to the same inputs in KernelTheory::LeanReference (Lean's kernel exactly: its Nat literal extensions and no Clean reducer). A reducer that never fires is not covered. It also requires the battery to FIND the disagreement for String.drop/take/trimLeft/trimRight/toLower/toUpper and BitVec.ofNat, and that no non-Nat reducer is admitted without being listed. Measured with the round-1 binary: every .olean re-check lane accepted `"abc".drop 1 = "xbc".drop 1`, `"\u3000x".trimLeft = "x"`, `"Ä".toLower = "ä"` and `"ß".toUpper = "SS"` by rfl, all false in Lean 4.30.
